column3: “I will go to give rest to it” is rendered “when it went to find its rest.”
The Hebrew says “to me”; NASB has “to him,” following the LXX. NASB supplies “saying.”
“On the chief of the nations” is rendered “among the chiefs of the nations.”
“Bring them” is rendered “lead them,” and “lead them” as “make them walk.”
“There will be a reward for your work” is rendered “your work shall be rewarded.”
“Slapped on a thigh” is rendered “smote on my thigh.”
“They are moved, my inward parts” is rendered “My heart yearns.”
“Surround” is rendered “encompass”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Farmers and they will journey” is rendered “the farmer and they who go about.”
“Give water to the throat of the weary” is rendered “satisfy the weary ones.”
